<codex_delegation>
  <source_thread_id>019f663b-6195-7130-8d2a-6bf5aaf24a8b</source_thread_id>
  <input>Make Doppler the governed source for TaxKit credentials and environment variables across local Bun development, Alchemy/Cloudflare deployment work, and GitHub Actions, while keeping secrets out of source control, logs, caches and evidence files.

At the start, read the repository-local AGENTS.md, docs/README.md and all task-owning architecture, operations, standards, runbook, SPEC and execution-plan documents. Immediately use the goal tools to establish this whole request as the task’s governing parent goal. Do not create a duplicate if an unfinished parent goal already exists.

Work through this as one end-to-end task:

1. Research before proposing changes. Thoroughly inspect the current TaxKit implementation and the working Doppler patterns in /Users/cooper/Projects/bundjil and /Users/cooper/Projects/site. Search other relevant sibling projects under /Users/cooper/Projects for useful, current examples. Compare how they handle Doppler projects/configs, local Bun commands, environment selection, Alchemy and Cloudflare inputs, GitHub Actions, service tokens, secret redaction, developer onboarding, CI caching, preview versus production separation, and recovery. Check installed package and CLI versions and use current official Doppler, Alchemy, Bun, GitHub Actions and Cloudflare guidance where needed. Record exact versions and reference revisions used. Treat reference repositories as evidence only: do not copy their local paths, private names, secret values or repository-specific assumptions into durable TaxKit files.

2. Draft the PRD/SPEC. Fully use the repository-local prd-writer skill. Define the present problem, ownership model, environments, trust boundaries, credential lifecycle, least-privilege access, bootstrap flow, failure and recovery behaviour, migration plan, test/proof requirements, rollout slices, explicit non-goals and a machine-readable task ledger. Prefer a small end-to-end vertical slice first, then extend it. Avoid unnecessary machinery.

3. Review it before implementation. Fully use the repository-local prd-review skill and revise the SPEC until it is coherent, testable and consistent with TaxKit’s architecture, authority model and documentation rules. Do not treat the first draft as approved merely because this task requested implementation; complete the review and record its outcome.

4. Implement the reviewed SPEC. Fully use the repository-local prd-implementer skill. Also follow docs-maintainer, strict-effect-ts, alchemy-iac and repo-structure for every relevant slice. Preserve the existing native Alchemy design. Use typed and decoded configuration boundaries, redacted secrets, clear environment ownership and secret-negative observability. Keep host scripts and workflow adapters narrow. Do not weaken current deployment proof, preview/production controls or repository checks.

5. Verify and close out. Test local Doppler-assisted Bun commands, the Alchemy configuration path, GitHub workflow behaviour through deterministic tests or safe hosted proof where authorised, missing/malformed configuration, secret-negative logs and receipts, preview/production isolation, and documented recovery. Run focused checks after each slice and the full repository verification at closeout. Update the SPEC, task ledger, active/completed execution plans, canonical architecture, operations docs and runbooks in the same slices. Commit coherent work, open and merge the required pull request to main when checks pass, then confirm exact origin/main identity and hosted check results.

Repository implementation and pull-request/merge work are approved by this request. Do not publish packages, change DNS/domains, deploy unrelated resources, expose secrets, or create/rotate/revoke Doppler, GitHub or Cloudflare credentials without the explicit operation-specific authority required by docs/operations/authority-model.md. If a provider mutation is genuinely needed, finish every safe repository and planning step first, then present the exact principal, resource, environment, change, rollback and readback needed for approval.

Finish only when the reviewed SPEC is implemented as far as current authority allows, all remaining exceptions are named and bounded, and the task provides a plain-English summary of what changed, what was proved, what remains, and what was deliberately not claimed.</input>
</codex_delegation>

Research completed read-only on 28 August 2026. I did not inspect any credential value or change any provider.

## Recommended TaxKit design

### Local Bun development

- Commit only a `doppler.yaml` mapping to TaxKit’s Doppler project and personal development config. Doppler documents `dev_personal` as a private config intended for each developer. The file contains project and config names, never secret values. [Doppler branch configs](https://docs.doppler.com/docs/branch-configs)
- Run `doppler login --scope=./`. Doppler otherwise scopes the login token to `/`, which lets every directory below it use that token. [Doppler CLI repository](https://github.com/DopplerHQ/cli)
- Run `doppler setup --no-interactive` from the repository root. Doppler stores the path mapping outside the repository. Moving the checkout requires setup again. [Doppler secrets setup guide](https://docs.doppler.com/docs/secrets-setup-guide)
- Governed commands should use:

  ```text
  doppler run --no-fallback -- bun run --no-env-file <script>
  ```

  `--no-fallback` stops Doppler writing or reading its encrypted secret snapshot. This matters because a revoked service token can otherwise continue using previously cached secrets. [Doppler fallback files](https://docs.doppler.com/docs/automatic-fallbacks), [Doppler service tokens](https://docs.doppler.com/docs/service-tokens)

- `--no-env-file` stops Bun loading `.env*` files, leaving the injected process environment as the single source. Bun otherwise loads several `.env` variants automatically. [Bun environment variables](https://bun.sh/docs/runtime/environment-variables)
- Do not pass tokens as command-line arguments. GitHub warns that command arguments can be visible to other processes, especially on self-hosted runners. [GitHub secure use reference](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/security/secure-use)

One important local finding: Doppler CLI 3.76.5 first tries the system keyring, but its exact source falls back to saving the token in its mode-`0600` configuration file if keyring storage fails. TaxKit onboarding should verify that the stored entry is a `secret-…` keyring reference and fail closed otherwise. [Doppler CLI 3.76.5 source](https://github.com/DopplerHQ/cli/tree/3.76.5)

### GitHub Actions

Use the Doppler secrets-fetch action directly:

```yaml
uses: dopplerhq/secrets-fetch-action@451892f16195f9ac360e1a5bcbf0b5fd0e957534 # v2.0.0
```

That action supports OIDC, service-account tokens and single-config service tokens. It masks fetched values except Doppler metadata and values deliberately marked `unmasked`. It can expose values as individual step outputs. [Doppler secrets-fetch action](https://github.com/DopplerHQ/secrets-fetch-action/tree/451892f16195f9ac360e1a5bcbf0b5fd0e957534)

TaxKit requirements:

- Leave `inject-env-vars` unset or `false`. Doppler warns that enabling it gives every later process in the job access to every fetched value. [Doppler action usage](https://github.com/DopplerHQ/secrets-fetch-action/blob/main/README.md)
- Pass only the named outputs needed by each exact Alchemy, Wrangler or proof step.
- Fetch credentials after dependency and browser caches have been restored and saved. Never cache after secrets enter the job.
- Never include Doppler, Alchemy or provider credential directories in cache or artifact paths.
- Do not print the environment, enable shell tracing, upload raw plan output without filtering, or write secret values or secret hashes into evidence.
- Keep each sensitive value separate. GitHub says masking structured JSON, YAML or XML secrets can fail because masking relies mainly on exact value matching. [GitHub secure use reference](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/security/secure-use)
- Pin the action to the full SHA. GitHub says this is the only immutable way to use an action. [GitHub secure use reference](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/security/secure-use)

Preferred authentication is Doppler service-account identity through GitHub OIDC. It avoids a permanent Doppler token in GitHub. It needs `id-token: write`, exact audience and subject rules, and a Team or Enterprise Doppler plan. Doppler says to avoid wildcard claim matching. [Doppler service-account identities](https://docs.doppler.com/docs/service-account-identities)

Use separate identities and config access for Preview and Production. Bind each identity to its protected GitHub environment. Before configuring it, read the live OIDC subject. GitHub changed the default subject format for repositories created after 15 July 2026 to include immutable owner and repository IDs, so old examples may be wrong for a new repository. [GitHub OIDC reference](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/openid-connect-reference)

Creating those identities is an external provider change and needs separate authority.

The safe temporary fallback is one read-only Doppler service token for each config, stored as the only GitHub environment bridge secret. A service token is scoped to one config and can have an expiry. Do not grant its optional write access. [Doppler service tokens](https://docs.doppler.com/docs/service-tokens)

### Alchemy and Cloudflare

TaxKit uses Alchemy `2.0.0-beta.64`. Its Cloudflare provider reads:

- `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` through Effect `Config.redacted`
- `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID` as a required ordinary configuration value

It fails when the account ID or credentials are missing. [Alchemy v2.0.0-beta.64 source](https://github.com/alchemy-run/alchemy/tree/v2.0.0-beta.64)

Keep the existing native design:

- Doppler injects the Cloudflare deployment inputs.
- Alchemy continues to own its internal state-store bearer token and encryption key in Cloudflare Secrets Store.
- Those internal Alchemy values are a named exception because they are generated infrastructure state, not TaxKit deployment inputs.
- Keep `CI=true`. In this mode Alchemy retrieves the state-store bearer for each run and does not write its local state-store credential cache. [Alchemy state-store documentation](https://v2.alchemy.run/state-store)
- Keep typed decoding before provider work and keep Cloudflare tokens wrapped as redacted values.
- Preserve explicit `prod` and `pr-<number>` stages. Alchemy stores their state and physical names separately. [Alchemy stages](https://v2.alchemy.run/environments/stages)

Cloudflare recommends account-owned API tokens for durable CI because they are not tied to one employee. Token creation requires the relevant administrator authority. Scope a token to the exact account and only proven permissions. [Cloudflare account API tokens](https://developers.cloudflare.com/fundamentals/api/get-started/account-owned-tokens/), [Cloudflare Workers CI authentication](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/ci-cd/external-cicd/github-actions)

Alchemy’s Cloudflare state flow specifically needs `Secrets Store Write` because it binds the state secret into a temporary edge-preview Worker. Do not copy Alchemy’s broad example permission list; measure TaxKit’s actual calls and remove unused KV, R2, D1, Queues, Pages, DNS and zone permissions. [Alchemy CI guide at the tested revision](https://github.com/alchemy-run/alchemy/blob/v2.0.0-beta.64/website/src/content/docs/environments/ci.mdx)

Cloudflare supports token expiry, IP restrictions, status verification, rolling and deletion. Any creation, rotation or revocation remains an operation-specific external change. [Create API token](https://developers.cloudflare.com/fundamentals/api/get-started/create-token/), [Cloudflare token API](https://developers.cloudflare.com/api/resources/accounts/subresources/tokens)

## Cache and evidence rules

GitHub says fork pull requests can read base-branch caches. Cache contents are not signed and restored files must be treated as untrusted. Secrets, credentials and tokens must never enter a cache path. [GitHub dependency caching reference](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/dependency-caching)

TaxKit should therefore enforce:

- cache restore and save before Doppler access;
- package and Playwright paths only;
- no `.doppler`, `.alchemy`, fallback, mounted-secret or temporary credential paths;
- no secret-bearing environment dump in artifacts;
- evidence limited to expected variable names, environment identity, source revision, action SHA, result and provider readback;
- no secret values, transformed values, prefixes, suffixes or hashes.

The current TaxKit ordering already saves Bun and Playwright caches before the deployment credentials are used. Preserve that order.

## Failure and recovery behaviour

- Missing Doppler authentication: fail before fetching configuration.
- Missing or malformed named values: typed decoding fails before Alchemy contacts Cloudflare.
- Doppler outage: fail closed because fallback files are disabled.
- Preview token or config: cannot select Production resources.
- Production token or config: only available through the protected Production GitHub environment.
- Rotation: validate the replacement through a secret-negative read, replace the bridge or identity, verify provider access, then revoke the old token.
- Revocation: takes effect immediately because no Doppler fallback is allowed.
- Recovery evidence records identities and results only.
- Existing Alchemy state recovery remains unchanged.

Its pinned action code downloads the current installer and current CLI, so the final CLI version can change without a repository change. The pinned secrets-fetch action avoids that extra moving part.
